chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, or someone else, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazid, who said:

I entered upon al-Rida عليه السلام while, at that time, I was a Waqifi. My father had asked his father about seven questions, and he answered him concerning six and withheld from the seventh. So I said: “By Allah, I will surely ask him about what my father asked his father; if he answers with the same answer as his father, that will be a proof.” So I asked him, and he answered with the same answer as his father had answered my father regarding the six questions. He did not add to the answer a waw nor a ya, and he withheld from the seventh.

And my father had said to his father: “I will contend against you before Allah on the Day of Resurrection that you claimed that Abdullah was not an Imam.” So he placed his hand on his neck, then said to him: “Yes, contend against me with that before Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. Whatever sin there may be in it is upon my neck.”

Then when I bade him farewell, he said: “There is no one among our Shi'a who is afflicted with an affliction or suffers a complaint and is patient upon that, except that Allah writes for him the reward of a thousand martyrs.” So I said to myself: “By Allah, there had been no mention of this.”

Then when I went on and was on part of the road, the vein of al-Madini came out in me, and I suffered severe pain from it. Then the following year I performed hajj and entered upon him while some of my pain still remained. I complained to him and said: “May I be made your ransom, seek refuge for my leg,” and I stretched it out before him. He said to me: “There is no harm in this leg of yours, but show me your sound leg.” So I stretched it out before him, and he sought refuge for it. Then when I went out, it was only a short while before the vein came out in me, and its pain was slight.

key_terms.أَجْرَ أَلْفِ شَهِيدٍ: The reward of a thousand martyrs granted for patient endurance
key_terms.بَلِيَّةٍ: An affliction or trial that befalls a person
key_terms.دَلَالَةً: A proof or indication establishing the truth of the matter
key_terms.عَوِّذْ: Seek protection or refuge for, meaning to recite for protection and healing
key_terms.وَاقِفِيٌّ: A follower of the Waqifi position at that time
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: The Day of Resurrection when people are held to account before Allah

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith present a proof for the Imamate of Imam al-Rida عليه السلام and the reward for patience in affliction?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts how al-Husayn ibn Umar ibn Yazid found a proof of the Imamate of Imam al-Rida عليه السلام through his exact correspondence with the answers of his father. It also includes a statement about the immense reward of patience during affliction for the Shi'a, and a narrated instance of the Imam's seeking refuge for healing.
